title: fix: web fetch silently changes JSON numbers
body:
## What Problem This Solves

`web_fetch` silently rounds JSON identifiers and high-precision decimals, turns large exponents into `null`, and rewrites negative zero as `0` before the model sees the response.

## User Impact

Models receive the server's exact numeric tokens, including `9223372036854775807`, `12345678901234567890`, high-precision decimals, `1e400`, and `-0`. Existing two-space JSON pretty-printing is retained so ordinary JSON output and truncation boundaries do not change. Content-type classification, malformed JSON fallback, size limits, external-content wrappers, and non-JSON responses are unchanged. No configuration change is required.

## Implementation

Keep the contributor's commits and use the native JSON reviver source context with `JSON.rawJSON` for numbers while retaining the existing serializer and indentation. Both APIs were exercised successfully in isolated Node 24.16.0 and 26.1.0 (the supported branch minima), Node 24.19.0 and 24.21.0 (CI versions), Node 26.10.0, and the repository-pinned OpenClaw Bun 1.4.3. A native runtime type declaration and optional callback context annotation bridge the missing ES2023 library typings without changing runtime behavior.

Thanks to @ly85206559 for reporting the problem, implementing the original fix, and adding HTTP regression coverage. The maintainer adjustment keeps main's formatting rather than returning source whitespace, avoiding an unrelated output change.

## Evidence

[Recorded main/candidate model-visible tool results, ordinary JSON formatting, and oversized truncation excerpts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170123#issuecomment-6133200601)

- Built main `31ec669615b9272b74b1b87ecf475d664f609bc9` and the candidate independently in secretless Docker.
- Ran `pnpm openclaw --profile ... agent --local` with a recording OpenAI-compatible provider. The provider called the registered `web_fetch` through `tool_call` against a loopback HTTP server and recorded the subsequent tool results.
- Main rounded the two large identifiers and the high-precision decimal, converted `1e400` to `null`, and converted `-0` to `0`. Candidate preserved every numeric token. The `0.30000000000000004` control remained exact on both.
- Ordinary JSON, HTML, and oversized JSON tool results were identical after normalizing timestamps, elapsed time, random wrapper IDs, and spill paths. Oversized JSON retained the same 122,909-character formatted source, 1,200-character output budget, truncation boundary, marker, and spill metadata.
- Focused HTTP fidelity, general web-fetch, output-contract, and header/extraction tests: 32 passed across four files in 23.29 seconds. Changed-file Oxfmt and Oxlint passed with zero warnings or errors; the isolated ES2023 native-API type probe passed. The structured `+json` header test retains main's pretty-printing expectation.
- Contributor's original [Gateway proof](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/38298834475) and [main-parent diagnostic replay](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/38304096928) remain available as prior-head evidence, not validation of this head.
- Real-provider smoke on the candidate completed through the CLI with GPT-5 mini (low reasoning): one request, expected `P170123_LIVE_OK` reply. The task-only credential was removed afterward.
- The five inherited extension-bundle failures were checked with one original failing file per bundle on main `31ec6696`: Codex dynamic tools (59 failures), Copilot attempts (75), memory reindex recovery (11), Codex authenticated context (2), and Codex native configuration (suite-load failure). Each reproduces `Runtime config is not prepared`; the changed JSON serialization branch neither initializes nor reads runtime configuration and is not reached by those failing preparation paths. These diagnostics are not passing test runs.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Merge Risk


Two-way door: reverting fully restores the prior behavior; no state, schema, configuration, or public API migration. Blast radius is model-facing JSON fetched by `web_fetch`; non-JSON extraction and fetch transport are unchanged.
